target_customer: Commercial and military users of geospatial data, initially oil and gas operators and US defense customers, later insurers.
problem: Satellite and spatial data sits in many silos and is hard to search, buy, combine and manage, so most organizations do not use it in operations.
business_model: B2B enterprise SaaS and data marketplace, later an API for insurance

founders.name: Rachel Olney
founders.background_notes: YC page lists her as the only founder. Profile sites mention Stanford and defense work, but I did not open a primary source, so education is left null.

competitors.name: Descartes Labs
competitors.what: Satellite-derived insights and a geospatial analysis platform
competitors.traction_then: Established player, same model as Orbital Insight per a 2017 review

competitors.name: UP42
competitors.what: Marketplace and platform for Earth observation data, formally launched September 2019
competitors.funding_then: Backed by Airbus Defence and Space

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating and serving large imagery catalogs and integrating many data sources is standard but data-heavy engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Reselling third-party imagery had thin lock-in; deeper workflow integration with government and insurers was the hoped-for moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Descartes Labs, an incumbent in the same space, bought Geosite's operating assets in April 2024; terms undisclosed.

market_need_then: Growth in satellites and sensors increased data volume while military and commercial buyers lacked unified access, per the company's YC description.

branding.domain_note: geosite.io; later redirected to Descartes Labs after the acquisition. A Brazilian firm also uses geosite.com.br.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic geo name, with an unrelated Brazilian company using the same name; no press about the brand. A US GEOSITE trademark was filed July 2018.

pivots.from: Marketplace for geospatial data aimed at oil and gas and defense
pivots.to: Geospatial API (Bedrock) and visualization tool (Ascend) for insurance
pivots.why: Not stated in sources; insurance focus described in coverage of the 2024 acquisition.

outcome_analysis: Geosite entered YC in Winter 2019 with a spatial data marketplace for oil and gas and defense, and later repositioned toward insurance with a data API. No funding round beyond seed could be verified, it was crowded by better-funded geospatial players, and Descartes Labs bought its operating assets in April 2024 for an undisclosed price. The factor choice is a low-confidence inference from the absence of reported later rounds.
notes: geosite.io now redirects (301) to Descartes Labs insurance pages. Seed amount conflicts across aggregators ($150K, $1.5M, $2M; also a $5M Series A in 2021 on one aggregator), all single-source and unverified, so no rounds recorded. Business Wire release returned 403 and the Bee Partners page 404; acquisition details rely on GeoWeek search coverage with deal date reported as 2 April 2024 by CB Insights. The Descartes Labs entry reflects the company as a 2017 peer; Geosite's own batch-era competitor list is limited to dated sources found. Founder education left null because only profile aggregators mention it. Update: the 2021-07 Series A of $5M is reported by a martechseries press release (led by Lavrock Ventures and NextGen Venture Partners, with Bee Partners and MS&AD Ventures) and is recorded. The 2019-03 seed rests on a single database (Seedtable) and its amount is left null because Seedtable ($150K) and StartupIntros ($2M) conflict. The release gives no total raised; aggregators give totals of $5.4M to $7.2M, so the gap is not resolved.
